verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.5 A-1: 'Home and End go to the first and last label; Enter or Space acts. Undo, redo and reset are visible buttons after the board in the tab order; the shortcuts u (undo) and r (redo) work only while focus is inside the board.' SPEC 4.0 History: 'redo puts it back'. SPEC 7.7 Accessibility row: 'keyboard-only scripts for T1, T4, T13' (it does not say what the scripts contain). These passages require the behaviour and permit no gap in its tests.
verdicts.evidence: Read at f07eec6. T13-keyboard.spec.ts has 3 tests. They press Tab, Shift+Tab, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Enter and u. They never press Home, End or r, and never press the Redo button. Line 121 only checks that Redo gets the focus in the tab order. The file's header claims only 'Tab, Shift+Tab and the arrow keys; Enter acts; u undoes'. T13.spec.ts mentions 'redo' only in its hook list at line 25, and grep finds no Home or End in it. T13.test.ts, M9.spec.ts and M10.spec.ts have no redo, Home or End. T13SatakeStudio.svelte:470 has its own redo, scrub(play.cursor + 1), which both the History button and the r shortcut call (onKeydown, lines 481-487). DecorationDiagram.svelte:88-95 has its own onKeydown. The shared Board.svelte tests (board-keyboard.spec, M42) do not reach either one. The lens's patches, read as text, change exactly these two places. Records checked: the P6-A3 plan, section 6, defines the keyboard script as two tests (paint, tau and lights; a composite move with u, then reset). It sends A-1 to 'keyboard script, axe, 320 pixels, and the owner's reading at G6'. Its section 5 line 207 still requires Home, End, u and r. 9.2 requires 'A-1 to A-12 hold' but asks for automation only of acceptance criteria. decisions/P6-A3.md, the MERGE entries 'P6 stage 6.2, P6-A3', 'P6-A3 reviewed; rulings' and 'P6-A3 and P6-A4 repaired after review', the P6-A3 review (item 6 checked Home and End by hand, item 4 checked redo by hand) and gate-G6.md (report commit d59af4a, which names f07eec6; row 'keyboard scripts for T1, T4, T13' passes with T13-keyboard 3 passed) record no decision to leave these keys untested. The known-and-decided list has no such item. There is no earlier phase 6 round report. Precedent: P5-RT-11-02, the same kind of gap, was not refuted in the phase 5 round. One part of the finding is wrong: its claim that 'every earlier board tool's spec presses Home or End' is overstated, since grep finds no Home or End in T03, T05, T06, T09, T10, T15 or T16.spec. This does not affect the cause.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because 7.7 leaves the script's contents open and the plan sends part of A-1 to the owner, but no sentence permits a T13 whose Redo, r, Home and End can be removed with every test still passing. A-1 and 4.0 require them, and plan line 207 names them. R2 failed, because the finding reads A-1, 4.0 and 7.7 correctly; only its aside about earlier specs is overstated. R3 failed, because T13 is phase 6 and the gate is G6. R4 does not apply. R5 failed, because 7.5 has no [D] mark, the 4.0 [D] binds the build, and no fragment records the gap. R6 failed, because gate-G6.md and the earlier records hold nothing on it. On severity, the rubric does not clearly name the case. It falls between 'a test that could be stronger without being wrong' (the build works; review item 6) and 'a test suite that passes while the behaviour is absent', and the RT-11 lens file's attack 18 grades a surviving keyboard-script mutant as blocker. So major stands.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.5 A-10: 'every tool has a "show as table" view that presents the same state as an HTML table with a button per node'. CONTRACTS 5.1 ToolFrame: '"Show as table" toggle whose table has one button per node (A-10)'. COMMON 4.3: 'A test must fail when the behaviour it guards is removed'. These passages support the finding.
verdicts.evidence: Read at f07eec6. T13SatakeStudio.svelte:903 (data-table-node, onclick paint) and :935 (data-table-restricted, onclick compositeMove) are the two table actions. decisions/P6-A3.md 'the panels and the history' records them as the design ('one paint button per node', 'the restricted board with one button per node'). The T13.spec.ts header (line 27) lists 'table view: data-table-node (the paint buttons), data-table-restricted' among the hooks it reads. The file never uses either attribute. Its only table checks are in the no-JavaScript test: a details table is present (line 519) and it has at least 3 buttons (line 520). git grep over site/tests finds data-table-node or data-table-restricted for T13 nowhere else. T13-keyboard.spec.ts, T13.test.ts and M9.spec.ts do not touch the table. Records checked: the P6-A3 plan's section 6 says '"show as table" (the no-JavaScript test reads the table view)'. That assigns a presence check and does not say the buttons need no test. 9.2 asks only that a tool 'has a "show as table" view'. 9.5 Risks lists 'table view, manual testing at each release' as a mitigation, not as an exemption. The DECISIONS MERGE entries on P6-A3, the P6-A3 review (it opened the table view only for axe and 320 px), gate-G6.md and the known-and-decided list record no decision on testing the table buttons. One part of the finding's comparison is incomplete but harmless: T02 and T08 count their table buttons without clicking them, while T01, T03 to T07, T09 to T12 and T15 click theirs.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because A-10 calls for a button per node that presents the tool's state, and no sentence permits buttons that can do nothing; the plan's presence check is not a permission. R2 failed, because the finding reads A-10 and COMMON 4.3 correctly, and the spec's own header claims to read data-table-node and data-table-restricted but never does. R3 failed, because T13 is phase 6 and the gate is G6. R4 does not apply. R5 failed, because A-10 has no [D] mark and no fragment records the gap. R6 failed, because nothing is on record in gate-G6.md or earlier rounds. Minor matches 'a test that could be stronger without being wrong': the table view exists and the build's buttons act.

verdicts.citation: build-plan/COMMON.md 4.4: forbidden, 'a golden value typed into source'. The T12.test.ts header says 'Every value expected below is read from the golden file or computed by the engine; the only matrices typed are the worked values of the instruction'. The RT-11 lens file, section 6, allows only the listed SPEC literals (2.8, A.1, 2.11, 7.3, 7.5) 'with a comment naming the section'. These support the finding.
verdicts.evidence: Read at f07eec6. T12.test.ts:1329 has expect(e6).toMatch(/... data-format="grid" data-rows="27"/). Line 1331 has the same with data-format="list" data-rows="56". Line 1444 has expect(h).toHaveLength(27) for buildRepresentation(E6, 1). None of the three has a section comment. Oracle values, from python3 -I on the gate's golden_data.json copied to scratch: minuscule_representations[type=E6;node=1].dimension = 27, [type=E7;node=7].dimension = 56, types.E6.fundamental_orbit_sizes[0] = 27, types.E7.fundamental_orbit_sizes[6] = 56. So these are golden values, typed. The regression test (T12.test.ts:1782-1791, '// regression: P5-RT-11-03') greps only toBe(24|8|6|240|576|56), toHaveLength(1792|576) and expectedItems: 56 in the unit file. It cannot see data-rows="N" or toHaveLength(27). Yet its title says 'read the golden orbit sizes and dimensions instead of typing them'. The three lines already stood at 006f50d (lines 1289, 1291, 1404), and the phase 5 finding's grep, listed lines and the RT-FIX record (DECISIONS.md and decisions/RT-FIX-P5-t12-a11y.md, which carry only the environment entry naming P5-RT-11-03) did not name them. So this is a sibling of P5-RT-11-03 that the fix left, not a regression of a fixed line. That does not change the cause. SPEC 4 T12 prints 'above dimension 27' as the grid rule, and the P5-A2 plan line 203 names tests for 'dimension 56' and 'dimension 27'. But T12 and the plan are not in the lens's literal list, no line carries the section comment, and 56 and the header count at line 1444 are dimensions, not the threshold. T13.spec.ts line 225 is not relevant; the finding itself says T12.spec.ts:225 reads goldenDim.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because the SPEC T12 '27' is the grid threshold, not in the lens's list of allowed literals and carrying no section comment, and 56 and line 1444's count are golden dimensions. R2 failed, because the cause stands under COMMON 4.4 and the file's own header; that the phase 5 grep never covered these lines shifts the 'fix partial' framing, not the cause. R3 failed, because T12 is phase 5 and the gate is G6. R4 failed, because the oracle gives 27 and 56, equal to the typed values, so this is a provenance defect, not a mismatch. R5 failed, because no [D] mark covers it and nothing is recorded, and the 'typed numbers kept in brace strings' item concerns lesson prose. R6 failed, because the regression test of P5-RT-11-03 does not cover these lines and nothing records them as open. Minor matches 'a test that could be stronger without being wrong', as in phase 5.
